trips.introduction: A list of trips I've taken.

trip.comments: Surprisingly, this was our first stay in Annecy, even though we live only an hour and a half away from it. Some of the activities we did during our stay: Château de Menthon-Saint-Bernard, swimming in the lake, Fort Boyard Aventures, boat trip (Annecy-Doussard), cycling halfway around the lake (Doussard-Annecy), and a license-free electric boat (max 6 km/h). The area very clearly suffers from overtourism and is somewhat choking on its car traffic, even as it promotes cycling.
My first time in Croatia and also my first (but probably not last) trip to Venice. In Croatia, we visited Dubrovnik, Trogir, Split, Zadar, Šibenik, Krka, Rovinj, and Pula.

My first trip to Paris in 17 years. We visited a few tourist hotspots (Montmartre, Sacré-Coeur, Notre-Dame). I think I took a bateau-mouche for the first time in my life. We also visited the Lee Miller exhibit at the Musée d'Art Moderne and saw Le Roi Lion at the Théâtre Mogador.

We stayed 4 nights at the Aqua Dome in Oberlängenfeld, which we loved (nice hotel and baths, fantastic food). After a few days, we realized that we already went to the Aqua Dome back in 2011! We also went to the Neuschwanstein Castle.

We went back to the Zoological Gardens (Basel Zoo) and the Spielzeug Welten Museum (Toy Worlds Museum), which we visited also with our son more than 5 years ago. He didn't remember it. We also visited the fantastic Yayoi Kusama exhibition at the Fondation Beyeler.

We went to the Dolder ice rink (very fun!), we returned to Haus Hiltl, the world's first vegetarian restaurant (1898), we visited Zauberpark and its light installations, and we also visited the Titanic exhibition at the Lichthalle MAAG, among other things.

A 2-day trip to Milan. I went there mainly for a KNOWER concert, but I also visited the Cathedral (Duomo), the Teatro alla Scala Museum, the Pinacoteca di Brera, the Museo del Novecento, the Sforzesco Castle courtyards, and the Parco Sempione.

My 7th visit to Europa-Park, the 3rd one with our 7-year-old son, who now had access to more roller coasters: Wodan (2012), Poseidon (2000), Matterhorn-Blitz (1999), and Swiss Bob Run (1985). We went to Aquabasilea on our way to Rust.

trip.pictures: Québec: Lac Thomas, Mauricie & La Tuque
Québec: Lac Gamelin, Lac Saint-Jean & St-Félicien
trip.comments: My 3rd trip to Québec and 4th trip to Canada (5th, counting a brief visit of Niagara Falls back in 2001). We visited Montréal, Québec, La Mauricie National Park, the Lake Saint-Jean, Saguenay, and Tadoussac areas. We stayed at two lakeside chalets, which was very nice. We also saw Mike Stern at the Festival International de Jazz de Montréal. I'm still fascinated by the far north areas, which we have never visited - and which probably are more boring in practice than in theory. Still, I'd really like to visit one of those towns in the North part of Québec someday.

A pretty packed trip to Rome, including visits to: the Trevi Fountain, Trastevere, the Colosseum (with the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill), the Pantheon, the Galleria Borghese, the Papal Basilica of Saint Mary Major, the Catacombs of Callixtus (San Callisto), the Vatican (Saint Peter’s Basilica, the Vatican Museums, and the Sistine Chapel), the Palazzo Colonna, and Piazza Navona. We also saw the temporary exhibition "Picasso lo straniero" at the Palazzo Cipolla. This wasn’t planned, but visiting Saint Peter’s Basilica also meant seeing Pope Francis' remains. This was my first trip to Rome since 2004 (Keith Jarrett concert, Colosseum, Vatican Museums, Trevi Fountain, etc.).

A very short stay in the Charmey and Gruyères region. It was the second time I went to the thermal baths of Charmey, the second time I visited the Gruyères Castle and the second time also that I went to the Maison Cailler. The first time I actually visited the inside of the Gruyères Castle was in 2011 and the first time I went to Charmey and the Maison Cailler was in 2017.
Our 6th time in Basel. We visited the Naturhistorisches Museum, Tinguely Museum, and Beyeler Foundation (Matisse - Invitation to the Voyage).

Possibly my first time in Zürich since 2009. In the past, I mainly went there to see concerts: Prince in 1998 and 2002, Marcus Miller in 2002 and 2005, Keith Jarrett in 2009. For some reason, we also saw David Copperfield at the Hallenstadion in 2005 (I was not impressed). This time, I particularly liked the Altstadt and the Kunsthaus (Matthew Wong - Vincent Van Gogh exhibition). We also passed by Kaufleuten, the club where I shook Prince's hand in 2002, among other things.

Our 6th stay in Leukerbad and our 3rd at the Bristol Hotel. We took the Gemmi cable car and did a small hike from the top (there was a lot of snow). We should do a longer hike in the area the next time we go there (e.g. Kandersteg).

Our first time on the Île de Ré. A very nice island. We obviously did a lot of cycling (that's what people do there). Some places we visited on our way to the island and back: Guédelon, Zoo de Beauval, Château de Chenonceau, Puy du fou, Tours, and Dijon.
My 19th trip to Berlin. Our first trip with our son and my parents. This year, our focus was on landmarks, since 3 persons were discovering Berlin for the first time.
Our 6th visit to Europa-Park. 3 days. 2 nights. It was a blast. We met several friends and their children. This was also our longest trip with our VW ID.3.

My first time in the UK outside of London. We visited Canterbury, Brighton, Portsmouth, Salisbury, Bath, and Oxford. I didn't know anything about most of those places, so that was an enriching trip. Stonehenge was a highlight, but there were many things to like, from cathedrals/abbeys to old warships. I was also pleasantly surprised by the fact that vegetarian/vegan dishes are available in most restaurants. This is not something you see often in Swiss restaurants...
My first time in Corsica. We stayed in the Ajaccio, Porto-Vecchio, and Bonifacio areas. Beautiful landscapes, mountains, beaches, etc. I hope we'll have the opportunity to return there one day.

My 3rd trip to London. The 1st time, in 2003, was to see Keith Jarrett at the Royal Festival Hall. The 2nd time, in 2007, was to see Prince at the O2 and at the Indigo2. This time, we didn't see any concert, but we saw a play (The Mousetrap), a musical (Back to the Future: The Musical) and visited three museums (Tate Modern, British Museum, and National Gallery), among other things. That was fun. I will miss the vegetarian/vegan restaurants, like in Berlin.

Our 5th trip to Basel and 5th visit to Europa-Park, this time with our 4-year-old son. In Basel, we visited the Basel Paper Mill, which is a fantastic place for children (and adults!), and went to Aquabasilea.

trip.place: Le Boucanet / Montpellier / Carcassonne / Toulouse, France
trip.image: 2022-07-27 Le Boucanet - Montpellier - Carcassonne - Toulouse, France.jpg
trip.comments: My first time in all those nice places. I'd like to go back to Toulouse someday, but probably during spring or fall, when it is less hot.

Turin and Milan both have beautiful areas, but Verona was our favorite place visited during this trip. We'll probably visit it again in the near future. Possibly in spring/autumn, as the temperatures were too high for my taste. Stresa and the Borromean Islands were also very nice, with the advantage of being quite close to where we live (i.e. also an idea for an upcoming weekend).

This was our first time in Weil am Rhein and our 4th trip to Basel. We had an excellent meal (vegan menu, for me) at Gasthaus zur Krone. We visited the Beyeler Foundation, the Vitra Campus, the Kunstmuseum Basel, and Augusta Raurica, among other things.

My 18th trip to Berlin (my 4th since 2010 actually). This was a trip to mark our 10 years of marriage, as Berlin is a special city for us. We visited the Humboldt Forum for the first time (twice), among other museums. We planned two special diners at a vegetarian (Cookies Cream) and vegan (Lucky Leek) Michelin restaurants, and visited some of our favorite "normal" restaurants as well (Atame, Samadhi, and Oxymoron). We also biked quite a lot. That was fun.

I might have already visited Schaffhausen, Saint Gall, and the Grisons when I was a child, but I'm not sure. It would have been a very long time ago. Anyway, Switzerland is expensive, but it's also beautiful. We should probably go back to the Grisons once our son is older, so we can hike and bike there.
A family trip in Vallorbe (Vallorbe Caves), Bern, Lucerne (Swiss Museum of Transport), and Interlaken (rain, mostly).

Our fifth stay in Leukerbad and our second at the Bristol Hotel, which has its own indoor and outdoor thermal bath. It was a welcome break, without our almost-3-year-old son. Being able to go to a bar and a restaurant for the first time in four months was also pretty cool.

Our third weekend in Basel (and our first with our 2-year old son). We went to the Spielzeug Welten Museum, among other things (walking in the Old Town, crossing the Rhine on small boats, having delicious food at Markthalle, etc.). This certainly won't be our last stay in that nice city.

This was my first trip to Bretagne / Brittany in about 30 years. I didn't swim in the English Channel (La Manche), this time (one story I heard a lot those last 30 years: I apparently was almost taken by strong currents when swimming in La Manche in St-Malo - I didn't realize at the time I could have been in danger). We ate a lot of crêpes (sometimes because it was the easiest way to eat something vegetarian), a lot of pastries (kouign-amann and others), and drank a lot of cider. If it wasn't for the non-vegetarian-friendly food (seafood and French cuisine in general), I guess I could live in Brittany. This is a really nice region.
Our fourth stay in Leukerbad (after 2006, 2014, and 2018). Our first weekend without our 16-month-old baby.

I already visited Oslo in 2002, but this was the first time I visited Northern Norway. We had a lot of luck with the weather (a lot of sun, comfortable temperatures, often around 20 °C). North Cape (Nordkapp) was a bit underwhelming (it's a place "at the end of the world", but it somehow looks fake/artificial). I'm glad we went to Magerøya (the island), though. I really like sparsely populated areas. The Lofoten Islands were absolutely fantastic, of course. I'd like to go back there again, someday, and visit Senja and possibly other islands as well.

trip.place: Cala Mesquida, Mallorca, Balearic Islands, Spain
trip.image: 2018-09-07 Cala Mesquida, Mallorca, Balearic Islands, Spain.jpg
trip.comments: We did a similar trip last year (in Alcúdia, more or less on the same side of the island, 50 minutes away from Cala Mesquida), this time with a 4-month-old baby. The plan was more or less the same: sleep, eat, go to the swimming pool or the beach, read books, etc. This time I finished five books (three of which I had started many weeks ago). I also did a short hike to Talaia de son Jaumell (beautiful view). I think I prefered Cala Mesquida to Alcúdia (more nature, no cars, beautiful beach, mountains, etc.), but the hotel in Alcúdia (PortBlue Club Pollentia Resort & Spa) was probably a bit better than the one in Cala Mesquida (Zafiro Cala Mesquida). Next time, we should really visit the whole island more (with a rented car, possibly).

Our third stay in Leukerbad (after 2006 and 2014) and our last weekend/trip before our baby was born. Like last time, we had a massage at the Sources des Alpes (but we stayed at another, way cheaper hotel).

trip.place: Chicago / New Orleans / New York, USA
trip.pictures: New York: The Metropolitan Museum of Art of New York
New York: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
trip.image: 2017-10-07 Chicago - New Orleans - New York, USA.jpg
trip.comments: I had never been to Chicago. It's a nice city (lake, river, buildings, etc.). I particularly liked the Art Institute of Chicago (a fantastic museum!). It was the second time I went to New Orleans and the first time since 2001. This is the city I liked the least among the three. I liked the National WWII Museum, though. It's very well done. Finally, this was the third time I went to New York (after 2001 and 2004). A fantastic city, of course. The city. The Metropolitan Museum of Art is impressive. Probably one of the best museums in the world. The National 9/11 Memorial & Museum was completely different, but very moving and also very well done. It had a special meaning for me, as I first visited New York in September 2001, a few days before 9/11. I will also miss the vegan restaurants. A lot.

A weekend in Adelboden for our 5-year wedding anniversary. We stayed at The Cambrian, a wonderful hotel, with a beautiful view, a spa, an indoor pool, a small outdoor pool (warmer), an excellent restaurant, etc. A very relaxing stay. We visited Thun Castle on our way back.

This is not the kind of trips I'm naturally "attracted" to. We spent seven nights at PortBlue Club Pollentia Resort & Spa. We didn't visit the area. At all. Instead, we slept, ate, went to the swimming pool and to the spa, read books, etc. For six complete days. This was the plan and this is what we did. I finished A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy and started Homo Deus: A Brief History of Tomorrow. The last time we did something similar was in 2013, when we went to Fuerteventura.

trip.pictures: Tokyo: National Museum of Modern Art
trip.comments: This was a trip we had wanted to do for several years. It was obviously very different from our trip to Namibia in 2016: big cities (Tokyo, especially), many people (in the subway, in the stations, in the streets), a language (Japanese) we couldn't read, etc.; but it was also quite "exotic", in a different way. This was the cherry blossom season, so nature was still an important dimension of the trip, in a sense, although we mainly visited cities. It was quite a dense trip, which I see as a kind of introduction to a country I had never visited before. We definitely need to go back to Japan someday.
